newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil drops - good supply, mild weather.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil drops - good supply, mild weather.

text.p: NWE gas oil premiums weakened on Friday as good supplies and mild weather combined to exert downwards pressure.
Firmer futures for much of the day helped sweeten the pill for outright prices, but March IPE gas oil stumbled just before the close ending $1.75 a tonne down at $178.25.
Physical activity was muted with traders claiming required deals have been concluded ahead of industry functions next week.

Barges were under pressure almost from the start with Rotterdam refinery sold in the morning at March IPE +$3 fob ARA for second half February, compared with March IPE +$1 in the afternoon, $2-3 off Thursday's level. Traders said buyers were looking to pick up material at flat next week.
One trader, who was the market long before the Feb expiry, was seen as the main player in the market.
"They are trying to shift as much as they can," said one trader.
German grade heating oil, able to secure premiums of March IPE +$8.50 cif NWE and +$8.25 on the back of two cargo deals on Thursday, saw premiums slip to March IPE +$6 cif NWE for second half Feb.

FOD for second half Feb was also knocked lower, premiums slipping about $2 to March IPE +$2-4 cif NWE. First half March premiums, surprisingly were actually stronger at March IPE +$4-5, although the market was largely notional.

Diesel premiums, however, continued to gain some support for demand into France, part of it to cover refinery maintenance. Nothing was heard done, but premiums were pegged around March IPE +$20 for cif cargoes.
